rows: \(T/\mathrm K=\theta/{}^\circ\mathrm C+273.15\). A change of 1 °C equals a change of 1 K. Do not add the offset to a temperature interval.

Internal energy belongs to the system’s microscopic state. Heat is transfer caused by a temperature difference; work is another transfer mechanism. Neither is stored “heat”. Choose the system boundary.
\(\Delta E_{\mathrm{int}}=Q+W_{\mathrm{on}}=Q-W_{\mathrm{by}}\) when other stored-energy changes are negligible. Inward heat and work on the system are positive.

\(\Delta E_{\mathrm{int}}=C\Delta T=mc\Delta T\), with \(C\) in J/K and \(c\) in J/(kg K). Use an appropriate approximately constant capacity, fixed phase and sufficiently uniform temperature; include other energy changes when relevant.

\(T_f=\frac{C_1T_1+C_2T_2}{C_1+C_2}\). Positive capacities; common final temperature; no external heat, work or phase change. Include a vessel as another term if needed. The endpoint lies between the starting levels.

For a dilute ideal monatomic gas, temperature tracks mean translational kinetic energy per particle. Total internal energy also depends on particle number. This is not a universal microscopic formula for all materials.

\(v=\frac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt}\), \(a=\frac{\mathrm dv}{\mathrm dt}\). For \(x=x_0+v_0t+\tfrac12at^2\), constant \(a\) gives \(v=v_0+at\). A zero of velocity is a turn only if velocity changes sign.
Speed is \(|v|\). Away from \(v=0\), equal signs of \(v\) and \(a\) mean increasing speed; opposite signs mean decreasing speed. Displacement and distance are different.
\(v(t)\approx\frac{x(t+h)-x(t-h)}{2h}\), with \(h>0\) and both sample times inside the domain. Reducing \(h\) can reduce approximation error while amplifying rounded-input effects.
For initial speed \(v>0\), constant braking magnitude \(b>0\): \(t_A=\frac{v}{b}\), \(d_A=\frac{v^2}{2b}\). A constant-speed delay \(\tau\geq0\) adds \(\tau\) to time and \(v\tau\) to distance.
\(r_i=d_{\mathrm{observed},i}-d_{\mathrm{predicted},i}\); \(\mathrm{MAR}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_i|r_i|\). Keep repeated observations. Plot residuals as well as calculating a summary.

1 mph = 0.44704 m/s; 1 ft = 0.3048 m. A benchmark tests implementation. Observations test predictions under documented conditions. A smaller MAR alone does not identify a cause or validate a universal law.
code:
v = speed_mph * 0.44704
observed = distance_ft * 0.3048
predicted = v**2 / (2*b) + v*tau
residual = observed - predicted
mar = sum(abs(r) for r in residual) / len(residual)
